author: Justus Spitzmüller <74727117+sptzmllr@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Fix neighbour lookup to use correct 4-connectivity in fillminima (#88)

The previous implementation incorrectly added only diagonal neighbours
to the queue, ignoring directly adjacent pixels (up, down, left, right).
This could lead to checkerboard-like artifacts. The fix replaces the
nested loop with a simple 4-directional lookup using static offset
arrays.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Added compilation-failure test feature to CMake

Calling `alps_add_gtest(some_test COMPILEFAIL)` adds a test that
expects compilation failure in `some_test.cpp` when compiled with
`-DALPS_TEST_EXPECT_COMPILE_FAILURE`.

If the code guarded by
`#ifdef ALPS_TEST_EXPECT_COMPILE_FAILURE`...`#endif`
compiles successfully, the test code is supposed to return failure;
otherwise, the test will still fail, but it will not be recorded in
XML output.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Make params help available without setting description

If a parameter object is read from INI or constructed from
(`argc`,`argv`), it gets `--help` option automatically defined.

Calling `params::description(const string&)`  method also defines
`--help` if not already defined.

Default ctor does not define `--help`: empty parameter object is
indeed empty.

Side effect: if for some obscure reason one does not want to have
`--help` defined as a boolean option, there is no way to not have
it. One can always reassign a different type value to `p["help"]` or
erase it, but this will not change the auto-generated help message.

This should close #496.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Introduced selective builds of ALPSCore components

1. To exclude a component (and its testsuite) from being built, add
   it's name to CMake list `ALPS_MODULES_DISABLE` ::
        cmake .. -DALPS_MODULES_DISABLE=accumulators\;mc

2. If some component depends on a disabled component, the dependent component refuses to build.
   One needs to disable all dependent components explicitly.

3. The client code may inspect CMake list `ALPSCore_COMPONENTS` after
   `find_package(ALPSCore)` to determine if a component is available.

4. The cleint C++ code also has preprocessor symbols `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_*` defined,
   e.g. `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_GF` or `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_ACCUMULATORS`, if the corresponding
   component is built.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Remember Boost location and hint it to user's CMake

When configured, ALPSCore remembers the location of Boost that it
used. If a library user loads ALPSCore package before Boost,
`find_package(Boost)` will likely find the same Boost as was used by
ALPSCore. This behavior can be overridden by loading Boost prior to
ALPSCore.

Note that in many cases a library user does not need to find Boost
package, because ALPSCore provides transitive dependency on Boost
headers.

This addresses issue #391.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
New CMake variable setting `ALPS_CXX_STD`

Setting '-DALPS_CXX_STD=c++03` or '-DALPS_CXX_STD=c++11` chooses C++03
or C++11 standard, respectively. This choice is enforced on the client
code.

Together with enforcement of C++ compiler ID and version, this should
take care of C++ standard compatibility (unless the user tries to
override the standard in the client code).

This essentially addresses the issue #301.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Get rid of Find*.cmake altogether; make python component work too.

These last 2 commits address issue #113. The most significant changes:

1. To use the library, set `ALPSCore_DIR` environment variable to the
   ALPSCore installation root, and put in `CMakeLists.txt`:

    find_package(ALPSCore REQUIRED accumulators mc)
    # ...
    # the following is useful to ensure your code finds shared ALPSCore libs:
    set(CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH true)
    # ...
    target_link_libraries(my_prog ${ALPSCore_LIBRARIES})

  No need for ${ALPSCore_INCLUDE_DIRS} or compile definitions, the
  imported targets in `ALPSCore_LIBRARIES` should take care of them
  automatically (otherwise it's probably a bug!).

2. There are no more `Find*.cmake` packages to install. Everything is
   done using `*Config.cmake` files. The resulting install tree is
   (supposed to be) relocatable: it can be copied to another location
   and will still work.

3. The `*.pc` files were not touched, are not relocatable and may need
   fixing in the future.

4. `ALPS_ROOT` is no more used for usual installation.

5. In the case of component standalone builts, `ALPS_ROOT` can be set
   (as a CMake cache or as an environment variable) to hint the
   location of the installed ALPSCore components. It should not
   normally be needed if all components are installed in the same
   directory tree (that is, have common `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`).

author: Markus Wallerberger <mwallerb@umich.edu>
message:
Merge pull request #488 from mwallerb/hypot

Add Hypothesis testing support.

Adds `alps::alea::test_mean(x, y)`, which takes either one statistical result and a benchmark
or two statistical results, and returns the corresponding p-value.

For testing adds:

 * VAR(1) model (`alps::alea::util::var1_model`), a simple Markov process with a 
    finite autocorrelation length
 * Self test for `autocorr_acc`, which verifies the error bars and thus the autocorrelation length.

Fixes: #172

author: Markus Wallerberger <mwallerb@umich.edu>
message:
Change semantics batched estimator variance to weighted variance.

Previously, the batched (co-)variance estimates were trying to
estimate the ensemble (co-)variance, which means taking the
weighted variance and multiplying it by the batch size.

However, it is more natural for binning analysis and for
propagation of uncertainty to use the "true" batched variance.
This changes that.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Redesign of alps::params

Among essential changes:

1) No need to use `param["abc"].as<int>()`; simply `int i=param["abc"]`

2) If `T` is convertible to `U`, then for parameter `param["abc"]` of type `T` it is allowed to do `U x=param["abc"];`

3) List-type parameters can be declared as `define< std::vector<T> >(....)` and are assignable to `std::vector`

4) It is allowed to assign to an undeclared parameter, lile this: `T x; param["abc"]=x;`
   The parameter acquires type `T`, and cannot be declared via `define()` any more.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Static/dynamic building reworked.

New CMake flags:

* ``ALPS_BUILD_SHARED``: makes ALPSCore produce shared libraries by
  setting ``BUILD_SHARED_LIBS`` to ``ON`` in cache. Mutually exclusive
  with ``ALPS_BUILD_STATIC``.
* ``ALPS_BUILD_STATIC``: makes ALPSCore produce static libraries by
  setting ``BUILD_SHARED_LIBS`` to ``OFF`` in cache, and requesting
  static versions of Boost and HDF5. Mutually exclusive
  with ``ALPS_BUILD_SHARED``.
* If both ``ALPS_BUILD_SHARED`` and ``ALPS_BUILD_STATIC`` are set to
  ``OFF``, then no special request is done when requesting packages,
  and the libraries are generated as specified by
  ``BUILD_SHARED_LIBS``.
* A separate option ``ALPS_BUILD_PIC``, if ``ON``, requests building
  PIC code.

Note: MPI may still end up being linked dynamically!

author: Markus Wallerberger <mwallerb@umich.edu>
message:
Add interface for adding a bundle of data.

NB this is *not* the same thing as adding data with a weight; rather,
it is close to adding a bundle, which is assumed to have the count
associated.  The interface is thus protected, one might down the line
add a function like this:

    struct computed_bundle<T> { computed<T> src; size_t weight; };
    ...
    x_acc &operator<<(const computed_bundle<T> &src);

This is useful in (a) fixing the autocorr hierarchy; (b) re-use of
lower-lying results in `batch_result`.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Added compilation-failure test feature to CMake

Calling `alps_add_gtest(some_test COMPILEFAIL)` adds a test that
expects compilation failure in `some_test.cpp` when compiled with
`-DALPS_TEST_EXPECT_COMPILE_FAILURE`.

If the code guarded by
`#ifdef ALPS_TEST_EXPECT_COMPILE_FAILURE`...`#endif`
compiles successfully, the test code is supposed to return failure;
otherwise, the test will still fail, but it will not be recorded in
XML output.

author: Markus Wallerberger <mwallerb@umich.edu>
message:
Properly rescale (co-)variances before applying transform.

Also adds a test.

This issue is the side product of the fact that the variance of
a set of weighted measurements and the "ensemble" variance differ
by a factor, so we have to correct for that factor in the computation
of the variance, which means we have to undo that before we
transform that variance.  The clean solution would be to have a
"batching decorator" that makes this transformation.

Fixes: #506

message: 1. alps::Parameters object can now load an alps::hdf5::archive& object from either the constructor or the -- void load(alps::hdf5::archive & ar) --  function. It will by default look at all keys in the parent group / or the parameters group /parameters (added by me), which abides by the alps::params concept in the new NGS scheduler library. 2. On top of the alps::mcbase class in the NGS scheduler library, I add on 2 derived classes, namely alps::lattice_mcbase (analog to alps::scheduler::LatticeMCRun) and alps::lattice_model_mcbase (analog to alps::scheduler::LatticeModelMCRun). Unfortuantely, the NGS scheduler does not support the ALPS lattice and model libraries. Therefore, I need to keep a copy of alps::Parameters object, called this_copy_of_params_is_reserved_for_the_old_scheduler_library_which_is_to_be_depreciated in the alps::lattice_mcbase class. 3. I add on <qmc.ngs.h> under the folder <application/qmc>, of which a new class qmcbase (analog to QMCRun) which is derived from alps::lattice_model_mcbase, which is again derived from alps::lattice_mcbase, which is again derived from alps::mcbase class. This version is kept as similar to the QMCRun class as possible, but certain sockets to the NGS scheduler library are not suitable to the old scheduler library. The parts which do not socket well are commented out. This is needed for my directed-worm-algorithm (6th version) that is NGS and python-enhanced.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Enable request C++14 build; let client override C++ version

ALPSCore can be build with `-DALPS_CXX_STD=c++14".

Client may define, before `find_package(ALPSCore)`:

1) `set(ALPS_FORCE_CXX_STD ${std})`
                to request standard `${std}` when
                compiling targets that depend on ALPSCore;
${std} can be:
"C++11"  --- requests C++11
"C++14"  --- requests C++14
"custom" --- does not request anything; the compiler is governed
             only by user-set compiler flags.

2) `set(ALPS_FORCE_NO_COMPILER_CHECK true)`
                to ignore detected mismatch between ALPSCore's and
                cient's compilers.

This addresses issue #301.

message:
Cmdline overrides params restored from HDF5

If there is a single HDF5 file as a command line argument, the
parameters object is restored from that file. After that, the remaining `key=value`
pairs from the command line are parsed according to the types of the
values associated with the `key`s in the restored parameters
object. If parsing fails, exception is thrown.

This should close #436.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
This commit introduces the following environment variables that affect
`make test` (or `ctest`) behavior of ALPSCore:

| Variable                    | Default                 | Usual value    | Meaning |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------|----------------|---------|
| `ALPS_TEST_MPIEXEC`           | `${MPIEXEC}`             | `mpiexec`      | MPI launcher                                                      |
| `ALPS_TEST_MPI_NROC_FLAG`     | `${MPIEXEC_NUMPROC_FLAG}`| `-n`           | flag to specify the number of MPI processes                       |
| `ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC`         | 1                        | 1              | How many MPI processes to launch in MPI-enabled tests             |
| `ALPS_TEST_MPIEXEC_PREFLAGS`  | `${MPIEXEC_PREFLAGS}`    | (empty string) | MPI launcher arguments preceding the executable name              |
| `ALPS_TEST_MPIEXEC_POSTFLAGS` | `${MPIEXEC_POSTFLAGS}`   | (empty string) | MPI launcher arguments preceding the arguments for the executable |

The `${...}` above are CMake variables, normally set by `FindMPI` module.

Related: issue #211.

This should close #296.

Intended use:

**Case 1: Vanilla MPI-enabled environment.**

The command to run an MPI program using 2 processes: `mpiexec -n 2 some_test`

Setting the variables to run each MPI-enabled tests on 2 processes: `ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC=2 make test`

**Case 2: NERSC Cori**

(*Disclaimer:* not tested with an actual Cori run)

Users are not supposed to run `mpiexec`. One has to allocate interactive nodes first.

Allocating 2 Haswell nodes for 30 minutes: `salloc -N 2 -C haswell -q interactive -t 0:30:00`

Command to run on the allocated nodes: `srun some_test`

Setting the variables to run each MPI-enabled tests on the allocated nodes:
`ALPS_TEST_MPIEXEC=srun ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC=' ' ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC_FLAG=' ' make test`

(note the variables are assigned spaces, not empty strings!)

**Case 3: Blue Waters**

(*Disclaimer:* not tested on actual Blue Waters machine)

The `aprun` command is supposed to be used to launch parallel processes from an interactive node
(see https://bluewaters.ncsa.illinois.edu/using-aprun ).

Command to run on 16 cores, using 8 cores per node (that is, 2 nodes), placing the processes on adjacent cores:
`aprun -N 8 -d 1 -n 16 some_test`

Setting the variables to run each MPI-enabled tests with this configuration:
`ALPS_TEST_MPIEXEC=aprun ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC=16 ALPS_TEST_MPI_NPROC_FLAG='-N 8 -d 1 -n' make test`

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Remember Boost location and hint it to user's CMake

When configured, ALPSCore remembers the location of Boost that it
used. If a library user loads ALPSCore package before Boost,
`find_package(Boost)` will likely find the same Boost as was used by
ALPSCore. This behavior can be overridden by loading Boost prior to
ALPSCore.

Note that in many cases a library user does not need to find Boost
package, because ALPSCore provides transitive dependency on Boost
headers.

This addresses issue #391.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Make params help available without setting description

If a parameter object is read from INI or constructed from
(`argc`,`argv`), it gets `--help` option automatically defined.

Calling `params::description(const string&)`  method also defines
`--help` if not already defined.

Default ctor does not define `--help`: empty parameter object is
indeed empty.

Side effect: if for some obscure reason one does not want to have
`--help` defined as a boolean option, there is no way to not have
it. One can always reassign a different type value to `p["help"]` or
erase it, but this will not change the auto-generated help message.

This should close #496.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Making custom accumulator value types easier to use.

To use a custom value type, take `accumulators/test/custom_type.hpp`
as a template to follow. The idea is to define
`ALPS_ACCUMULATOR_USER_TYPES` before including `alps/config.hpp`, then
make sure that your value type follows the concept as described in the
`custom_type.hpp`. The methods marked as `@REQUIRED`,
`@REQURED_SEQUENCE` and `@REQUIRED_NONCONTINUOUS` are part of the
concept, the rest are implementation details.

This commit is the essence of resolution of issue #157: it is now
possible to define a custom type containing Eigen matrix in a similar way.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Introduced selective builds of ALPSCore components

1. To exclude a component (and its testsuite) from being built, add
   it's name to CMake list `ALPS_MODULES_DISABLE` ::
        cmake .. -DALPS_MODULES_DISABLE=accumulators\;mc

2. If some component depends on a disabled component, the dependent component refuses to build.
   One needs to disable all dependent components explicitly.

3. The client code may inspect CMake list `ALPSCore_COMPONENTS` after
   `find_package(ALPSCore)` to determine if a component is available.

4. The cleint C++ code also has preprocessor symbols `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_*` defined,
   e.g. `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_GF` or `ALPS_HAVE_ALPS_ACCUMULATORS`, if the corresponding
   component is built.

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Introduced versioning

...and moved MPI detection and config file generation around.

This addresses issue #347:

1. ALPSCore version is defined in `common/cmake/ALPSCommonModuleDefinitions.cmake`;

2. In the generated/installed ALPSCore code, the version is at `alps/config.hpp`
   as ALPSCORE_VERSION preprocessor symbol
   (will presumably need stringification to be used in C++ code);

3. The version has a standard CMake format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.TWEAK;

4. The versions with the same MAJOR are assumed to be backward-compatible.

Suggestions, especially what would be a more useful version format in
`alps/config.hpp`, are welcome.

options, except that there's no job file name.
In all scheduler classes, a new constructor was added, it accepts an instance

handling of the schedulers in the fitting precess much easier. The name of the
job file has to be added with the function set_new_jobfile(std::string),
which is implemented in MasterScheduler. The slave schedulers don't need the
job file name, they get the tasks directly from the master.
remote_worker.C contains the implementation for of 'get_summary' for remote
workers (forgotten in the last checkin).

author: Alexander <galexv@umich.edu>
message:
Cmdline overrides params restored from HDF5

If there is a single HDF5 file as a command line argument, the
parameters object is restored from that file. After that, the remaining `key=value`
pairs from the command line are parsed according to the types of the
values associated with the `key`s in the restored parameters
object. If parsing fails, exception is thrown.

This should close #436.

before linear regression. Also track the MAE instead of RMSE which is
more robust to outliers. Also fix bug where coefs are not restored if
calibration failed. Finally, deprecate centering the temperature
(meanTemp) -- this makes the coefficients less interpretable across
devices (temperature normalization changes the offsets too, making
comparisons across devices with different temperatures more cumbersome)

Closes #154

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
change output structure

Major change in how outputs are structured: When processing multiple
files, results are now grouped by subjects instead of results. As such,
specifying each folder for each result (e.g. timeSeries/, summary/) is
now deprecated. Instead, simply specify --outputFolder and all result
files will be stored there. The utilities writeCmds() and
collateSummary() were also modified accordingly to fit the new output
structure.

Example:

accDir/
    group0/
      subject001.cwa
      subject002.cwa
      ...
    group1/
      subject003.cwa
      subject004.cwa
      ...

writeCmds('accDir/', 'outDir/')
will result in the following output structure:

outDir/
    group0/
      subject001/
        subject001-summary.json
        subject001-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      subject002/
        subject002-summary.json
        subject002-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      ...
    group1/
      subject003/
        subject003-summary.json
        subject003-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      subject004/
        subject004-summary.json
        subject004-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      ...

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
major fixes/changes to sanDiegoFFT

Removal of 0Hz freq: The signal is substracted by the mean before
computing the FFT coefs to find the dominant frequencies. Otherwise,
the dominant frequency (p1, f1) will always be 0Hz, making these
features uninformative.

Fix spectral entropy: The calculation of the spectral entropy seemed
slightly wrong, using the magnitudes instead of the powers. There was
also some strange normalization applied (magDC = vmFFT[0] / max).
This is now fixed to correctly use the powers, and normalization is also
done correctly.

Fix p1, p33 (dominant powers): Again, these were using the magnitudes
instead of the powers as in the papers. A strange normalization is also
applied (dividing by max of the FFT coefs). This is now fixed to use the
powers. Instead of the strange normalization, use logscale to handle the
large values that p1, p33 tend to have.

Fix magnitude estimations (FFT0-FFT14): Magnitudes for 0Hz-14Hz (note:
this is different from paper's 1Hz-15Hz) were computed using Welch's
method, but the implementation had some mistakes. First, the running
window does not reach till the end of the signal, only until half of it.
Second, Welch's method uses overlapping windows. Another change in
the estimation is to use logscale instead of the strange normalization.

message:
native support for DST correction of CWA timestamp

Add native support to correct the CWA timestamps for potential
daylight saving time (DST) crossovers. To do this it keeps track of the
recording start time and its DST status, then for any subsequent
timestamp check if DST status has changed. If so, perform the
correction accordingly. For all this a timezone needs to be provided
(otherwise resolving DST wouldnt be possible) which defaults to
Europe/London.

All output files are now timezoned to UTC, although in the future it is
maybe preferable to convert it to the user-specified timezone, e.g.
Europe/London.

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
feat: add --minWearPerDay option to filter days with insufficient wear time

Add a new --minWearPerDay CLI option that allows excluding days with less
than a user-specified amount of wear time from summary statistics. This
addresses a common requirement in accelerometer research to avoid bias
from partial recording days.

Features:
- New --minWearPerDay argument supporting flexible time formats:
  * Hours: '20h' or '20H' or '20' (default unit)
  * Minutes: '1200m' or '1200M'
  * Days: '0.83d' or '0.83D'
- Per-day wear time calculation and filtering
- Excluded days are set to NaN for imputation but remain in time-series output
- New summary fields:
  * wearTime-numDaysExcluded: count of excluded days
  * wearTime-numDaysIncluded: count of included days
  * wearTime-minWearPerDayThreshold(hrs): applied threshold
  * day{N}-includedInSummary: per-day inclusion flag (0 or 1)

Changes:
- src/accelerometer/utils.py: Added parseTimeString() utility function
- src/accelerometer/summarisation.py: Implemented filtering logic in
  writeMovementSummaries() and updated getActivitySummary()
- src/accelerometer/accProcess.py: Added CLI argument and time parsing

Testing:
Validated with sample.cwa.gz data showing expected behavior:
- Days with <20h wear time correctly excluded from statistics
- Overall metrics adjusted appropriately (e.g., avg acceleration
  decreased 9.15% when excluding partial days)
- Maintains backward compatibility (all days included when not specified)

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
feat: add --minWearPerDay option to filter days with insufficient wear time

Add a new --minWearPerDay CLI option that allows excluding days with less
than a user-specified amount of wear time from summary statistics. This
addresses a common requirement in accelerometer research to avoid bias
from partial recording days.

Features:
- New --minWearPerDay argument supporting flexible time formats:
  * Hours: '20h' or '20H' or '20' (default unit)
  * Minutes: '1200m' or '1200M'
  * Days: '0.83d' or '0.83D'
- Per-day wear time calculation and filtering
- Excluded days are set to NaN for imputation but remain in time-series output
- New summary fields:
  * wearTime-numDaysExcluded: count of excluded days
  * wearTime-numDaysIncluded: count of included days
  * wearTime-minWearPerDayThreshold(hrs): applied threshold
  * day{N}-includedInSummary: per-day inclusion flag (0 or 1)

Changes:
- src/accelerometer/utils.py: Added parseTimeString() utility function
- src/accelerometer/summarisation.py: Implemented filtering logic in
  writeMovementSummaries() and updated getActivitySummary()
- src/accelerometer/accProcess.py: Added CLI argument and time parsing

Testing:
Validated with sample.cwa.gz data showing expected behavior:
- Days with <20h wear time correctly excluded from statistics
- Overall metrics adjusted appropriately (e.g., avg acceleration
  decreased 9.15% when excluding partial days)
- Maintains backward compatibility (all days included when not specified)

author: Aiden Doherty <aiden.doherty@bdi.ox.ac.uk>
message:
Substantial update to underlying Java code that extracts features from an epoch of x/y/z time series data.

The old EpochWriter.java file was almost 2,000 lines long, hard to follow, and had a lot of redundant code. This has now been amended as follows:
 - EpochWriter.java is now solely responsible for determining when enough values have been collected to form an epoch, and then determining the time and quality checks for that epoch

 - AccStats.java is then called to write basic summary statistics that we will always want e.g. vector magnitude such as ENMOtrunc and ENMOabs, x/y/z mean/std/range/covariance

 - Features.java is optionally called to write more elaborate features to support machine learning e.g. San Diego features, MAD features, Zhang/Rowlands features, and fourier features on x/y/z/vm channels. Here would be a good place to add in new features in future, and much easier for developers to find an easy entry place to the code

Other updates here include:
 - device.py now uses pandas to access stationaryPoints.csv file for calibration ... this allows explicit calls to the exact columns needed, rather than relying on numpy calls to specific column index ids

 - there is now just one Boolean variable called to extract features - before it was unwieldy to extract features for specific papers - the code is much cleaner as a result

 - the ordering of the columns in -epoch.csv.gz is now slightly changed. This helps keep the code easier to read, and doesn't have any effect on downstream programs which always rely on the column heading names rather than index positions.

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
auto download builtin ML models if not found

Download the builtin ML models during runtime if the model files are
not found. `--activityModel` flag is now to be interpreted as the builtin
model type to use (either `doherty2018` or `willetts2018`) rather than
the path to the model file. The code will then link to the corresponding
file via the dictionary `MODELS` in `accClassification.py`.

This change makes it easier to update our builtin models in the future
without having to notify the users to manually redownload the ML
models, and also `--activityModel` wouldn't need to change to the
updated path/filename. Instead, it will be on us to simply update
`MODELS` in `accClassification.py` to the new models.

Users can still use a custom activity model by supplying the path in
`--activityModelPath`. If supplied, then `--activityModel` is ignored.

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
change output structure

Major change in how outputs are structured: When processing multiple
files, results are now grouped by subjects instead of results. As such,
specifying each folder for each result (e.g. timeSeries/, summary/) is
now deprecated. Instead, simply specify --outputFolder and all result
files will be stored there. The utilities writeCmds() and
collateSummary() were also modified accordingly to fit the new output
structure.

Example:

accDir/
    group0/
      subject001.cwa
      subject002.cwa
      ...
    group1/
      subject003.cwa
      subject004.cwa
      ...

writeCmds('accDir/', 'outDir/')
will result in the following output structure:

outDir/
    group0/
      subject001/
        subject001-summary.json
        subject001-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      subject002/
        subject002-summary.json
        subject002-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      ...
    group1/
      subject003/
        subject003-summary.json
        subject003-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      subject004/
        subject004-summary.json
        subject004-timeSeries.csv
        ...
      ...

signal length.

message:
changes and improvements in unileverFeatures

Remove 0Hz frequency by substracting the mean signal before FFT. This
is to improve the estimated dominant frequencies since 0Hz will always
dominate otherwise.

Use power instead of magnitude to be consistent with the paper
implementation. Also use logscale for convenience to handle the large
values that they tend to have.

Increase precision of the returned values, since 3 decimals seems too
little.

Remove the optional computation of additional FFT coefs as this seems
to be never used.

message:
improve calibration

Improve calibration by taking into account outliers and removing them
before linear regression. Also track the MAE instead of RMSE which is
more robust to outliers. Also fix bug where coefs are not restored if
calibration failed. Finally, deprecate centering the temperature
(meanTemp) -- this makes the coefficients less interpretable across
devices (temperature normalization changes the offsets too, making
comparisons across devices with different temperatures more cumbersome)

Closes #154

author: Shing Chan <cshing.m@gmail.com>
message:
major refactor: improve checks, prints, cleanup

Rename variable 'rawFile' to 'inputFile' so that we dont confuse it with
'rawOutputFile', which is now named 'rawFile'. Similarly 'npyOutputFile'
is now simply 'npyFile'. Method 'processRawFile' is now called
'processInputFile'.
Use Python 'assert' to perform checks. Also simplify some checks,
e.g. ArgumentParser automatically checks for missing arguments.
Add new argument 'accProcess.py --npyFolder' for consistency.
Use 'os.path.join' to create paths. This properly handles both cases
whether a directory name is provided with or without the trailing
slash '/'.
Use 'atexit' to schedule deletion of intermediate files. This has the
benefit that it will still run if the code exits prematurely. Some
exceptions apply.
Slightly improve prints.
Highlight possible bug in accClassification.py where
MIN_TRAIN_CLASS_COUNT is not being used.
Commentary --not commented code-- to start with uppercase for slightly
better readability.

author: Michael Cayanan <michael.cayanan@jpl.nasa.gov>
message:
PDS-792 - Harvest: Handle Search Core config fields that need to go to a Registry to get values  (#67)

* PDS-792 - Harvest: Update Search Core configurations.

This updates how the tool populates Search Core fields that used to go
out to a Registry to get its values. They were denoted by a `.` period
character (i.e. instrument_ref.instrument_name). For instrument_name and
instrument_host_name, Harvest Policy config was updated to extract that
information from the label itself. For resources, it was decided to use
a lookup table to populate these fields. A script was created to get the
resources currently registered in Search. It can be run like so:

`%> python get_resources.py`

Output is a JSON-formatted file that contains the resource LID, the
resource_name and resource_url. This file is read in by Harvest at run
time.

author: Jordan H Padams <Jordan.H.Padams@jpl.nasa.gov>
message:
Registry and Harvest Hot Fixes merged from master (#89)

* PDS-796 Changed 'clean' mode to 'uninstall' (#79)

* PDS-822 - Harvest: Updated to register XPath Solr documents. (#80)

This update will post Solr documents containing a set of XPaths of the
entire label to a Solr collection named `xpath`. This will only occur if
the label blob was successfully registered.

* PDS-822: Update Search Service deployment with xpath collection (#81)

* PDS-822: Update Search Service deployment with xpath collection

updates includes modifications to the deploy script and the Dockerfile to
create a new collection for the xpath data.

Also includes some cleanup and streamlining of the installer script.

* Cleanup merge conflicts

* Cleanup script removing output comments

* PDS-804: Update Harvest and Search to for lid and lidvid fields (#82)

* PDS-804 - Harvest: Update config with lids

Previous Search Core config translated lid to identifier, but that is the wrong place to
do this. Instead, we will now ingest `lid` directly into the Search Service and update
the Solr config and schema to copy to the identifier field for the API.

* PDS-804 - Search: Update schema and config for lid/lidvids

* Update schema to copy lidvid and lid to identifier field for API
* Update solrconfig with new generateLIDVID updateProcessorChain to concatenate lid and version_id

* Update harvest example with inline comments (#83)

* Search: Lower heap space to 2GiB (#84)

Depending on your Docker/system RAM and physical memory, anything much larger than these
seems to crash Solr. This may be a safer bet.

* Update lidvid and identifier to be multivalued

* Fix typo with identifier field declaration

* PDS-831 - Harvest: Update how the tool versions products (#87)

* PDS-831 - Harvest: Update how the tool versions products

- Add the version id to the blobName when ingesting to the .system
collection.

- Set the `id` as the LIDVID when posting documents to the xpath
collection.

* PDS-831: Update solrconfig to use lidvid as uniqueKey

* PDS-849 / PDS-850: Update Registry for displaying latest product version (#88)

* PDS-849: Updated Registry search requestHandler for latest product

Solr provides the ability to perform a "group by" in a query:
https://lucene.apache.org/solr/guide/6_6/result-grouping.html

Using this as a template, we added various parameters to the default
query for the search/ and archive-filter/ request handlers, including:

* group = true - enable the grouping functionality
* group.field = lid - we have multiple versions of products based upon lids
* ground.sort = version_id desc - order groupings by version_id in descending order.
* group.format = simple - simplifies the format a bit for parsing
* group.ngroups = true - enable including number of groups in results. critical to getting a valid number of actual search results (not including older versions)
* group.truncate = true - enable this so the facets use the ngroups value not the actual number of products
* group.limit = 1 - default value we actually don't specify so it only shows the first value of the group

* PDS-850: Update XSLT to handle new Solr grouping

* Revert "Merge branch 'dev' into master"

This reverts commit 21f92d636869b5aaaa66714a3926b00eb82967f2, reversing
changes made to ec9d6de68f5fef6ce189ec98a76c37bed1ae0f72.

message:
Fix segfaults when invoking MPFR/MPC long double functions in mixed MSVC/MinGW environments.

The issue arises with the conda packages for MPFR/MPC, which have been compiled with
80-bit long double support. When we compile mp++ with MSVC, we have ABI issues because
MSVC uses 64-bit long double. We work around the problem by avoiding altogether the use
of long double APIs in MPFR/MPC, exploiting the fact that in MSVC double == long double.
